title: Proactive decode handoff onboarding guide
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a practical, operational onboarding and acceptance checklist for the new proactive decode handoff feature (a variant of speculative decoding that explicitly coordinates early token prefetch across kernel variants and KV cache partitions). The goal is to give SRE/Runtime engineers a repeatable set of tests, metrics and rollback controls for safely enabling the feature for a model family.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: runtime-level behavior when handoff is enabled for a model/version. Includes scheduler changes, kernel routing hints, KV cache namespace coordination, and fallback behavior when prefetch misses or kernel incompatibilities occur.
- Not in scope: multi-region routing policy (handled by routing layer), billing/quotas changes, and application-level prompt changes.

Glossary (brief):
- Handoff: when the scheduler decides to start generating speculative tokens on an alternate execution path (lighter kernel, lower precision) and later reconciles outputs.
- Prefetch seed: initial prefix tokens used to warm KV cache on alternate workers.
- Anchor kernel: the primary, high-accuracy kernel used for final output.
- Staging kernel: lower-latency or quantized kernel used for speculative prefetch.

High-level behavior summary:
1) On request arrival the normal path performs light analysis of sequence length, model flags, and cached prefix presence.
2) If prefetch conditions match policy, a handoff request is enqueued to a staging kernel pool to pre-warm KV entries for expected next-token prefixes.
3) The anchor kernel continues serving real tokens; when reconciliation point is reached, KV state is merged or invalidated according to versioning rules.
4) If staging kernel produced outputs used for early streaming, a confidence-check and deterministic reconciliation step verifies no semantic divergence beyond threshold.

Key design decisions captured for onboarding:
- Prefetch size cap: default 8 tokens but configurable per-model.
- KV namespace: use namespace-per-model-version + request-hash suffix to avoid cross-customer leakage.
- Merge policy: prefer anchor kernel KV if timestamps differ by >500ms; otherwise, accept staging edits only for cold cache misses.
- Determinism: reconciliation must never reorder tokens produced by anchor kernel; speculative outputs are advisory until anchor confirms.

Kernel routing and scheduling notes:
- Kernel selection hint keys: model_family, seq_len_bucket, avg_latency_ms, quant_profile. Scheduler attaches a route_hint when creating the handoff task.
- Pool sizes: start with 5% of total serving workers per model family as staging pool; metrics-driven auto-adjustment enabled after rollout.
- Backpressure behavior: if staging pool saturated, do not block anchor path — skip prefetch and mark request with metric tag prefetch_skipped.

KV cache coordination (practical rules):
- Key format: <model_version>::<request_prefix_hash>::<token_index>
- Eviction policy: LRU with per-prefix TTL 60s for prefetch entries; anchor write-through extends TTL to 300s.
- Concurrency: staging writes are tagged provisional=true. Anchor commits set provisional=false on successful reconciliation.
- Consistency window: during rollout, probes must verify that provisional reads never override committed values when anchor later writes.

Acceptance criteria (must pass these before enabling for 10% of traffic):
1) Correctness:
   - Determinism checks: for 1k synthetic prompts anchored against baseline, final outputs must match baseline (no handoff) in >= 99.5% of cases; documented acceptable diff types for the remaining.
   - Reconciliation fidelity: when anchor differs from staging, anchor result must be chosen 100% of the time and speculative stream must be reconciled cleanly.
2) Performance:
   - Median end-to-end latency improvement for cold-start requests >= 12% when handoff enabled.
   - 95th percentile latency must not regress by more than 5ms versus baseline.
3) Resource/cost:
   - Additional GPU cycles consumed by staging pool under steady load <= +6% of baseline.
   - Memory increase for KV provisional entries capped at +15% per node.
4) Safety:
   - No cross-tenant KV leakage observed in 100% of isolation tests.
   - No increased error-rate (5xx) attributable to handoff; if error-rate increases by more than 0.5% absolute, block rollout.

Metric collection and dashboards to create before rollout:
- prefetch_attempts (count), prefetch_successes (count), prefetch_skipped (count), prefetch_latency_ms (p95/p50), reconciliation_conflicts (count), provisional_kv_entries (gauge), anchor_commits (count), staging_gpu_util (pct), anchor_gpu_util (pct), e2e_latency_with_prefetch_ms (p50/p95).
- Dashboard: "Proactive Handoff - Safety" with error budget, conflict rate, isolation checks.

Automated tests and QA matrix (examples):
- Unit: KV provisional write/read semantics, key formatting, TTL changes.
- Integration: simulate staged writes followed by anchor commit under race windows (0ms, 250ms, 800ms).
- Performance: replay trace of 1M requests at scale in perf lab verifying 95th percentile and resource overhead.
- Isolation: synthetic multi-tenant simultaneous prefixes to ensure no cross-namespace reads.
- Fuzz: randomized prefix lengths and quant profiles to detect kernel incompatibilities.

Rollout plan (gated, measurable):
- Canary 0.1% traffic (internal only): smoke tests, smoke metrics stable for 24h.
- Canary 1%: run for 48h, run full acceptance suite in parallel on sampled traffic.
- Canary 10%: 7-day observation window, enable auto-scaling adjustments for staging pool.
- Progressive ramp to 50% then 100% only if all metrics within thresholds.

Rollback triggers and immediate actions:
- Trigger: reconciliation_conflicts spike > 0.2% sustained for 15 minutes.
  Action: Disable handoff via feature flag, drain staging pool, run remediation job to invalidate provisional KV entries.
- Trigger: 95th percentile latency > baseline + 10ms for 30 minutes.
  Action: Pause prefetching for largest models, reduce staging pool size by 50%.
- Trigger: cross-tenant read detected.
  Action: Emergency rollback to 0% and run forensics job (KV dump + audit). Notify security.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Identify impacted model/version from dashboard tags.
2) Toggle feature flag to off for that model.
3) Monitor anchor-only path for 30 minutes.
4) Re-run deterministic tests against sampled requests; if issue reproducible, create SEV and assign to runtime + applied-ml.

Example rollout-toggle CLI snippet (internal):
> rinfctl feature toggle --model redwood/m7-large --feature proactive_handoff --percent 10
> rinfctl observe metrics --dashboard "Proactive Handoff - Safety" --window 1h

Open questions and risk notes (short):
- How to best choose prefix-hash entropy to balance cache hit-rate vs memory overhead? Experiment: two strategies (request-hash vs ngram-hash) and compare hit/miss rate.
- Does provisional KV bust higher-level prefix caching? Need to coordinate with edge CDN layer.
- Calibration of confidence-check for streaming speculative outputs: should be model-specific threshold or learned per-customer?

Next steps (owners and rough ETA):
- Complete perf lab replay and update dashboard (owner: Marcus Chen, ETA: 2026-03-10).
- Add automated isolation test harness to CI (owner: Ava Rios, ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Finalize rollback scripts and runbook playbook (owner: Lina Park, ETA: 2026-03-03).

Notes to reviewers: this is operational-first: please focus feedback on observable signals, rollback clarity, and whether acceptance thresholds are conservative enough for enterprise SLAs.

Revision history:
- 2025-10-21: initial draft by Lina Park
- 2025-11-08: added KV provisional semantics (Marcus Chen)
- 2026-02-25: updated acceptance thresholds and metric names (Ava Rios)

(END)
